_readme: Expectations for the markdown fenced-block half of the `examples` Definition-of-Done gate
(issue #850) — see scripts/markdown-examples-gate.mjs. JSON has no comments, so keys that
begin with an underscore are documentation and are ignored by the gate.
Every other key is a repository-relative POSIX path, and each entry pins one ```logo block by
the SHA-256 fingerprint of its source — so prose edits above a block never churn this file,
but editing the block itself forces a re-triage.
Every entry is ASSERTED, not merely tolerated: the gate fails when a listed block stops
producing exactly these codes — including when it becomes clean (a stale expectation) — and
when a fingerprint matches no block in its file. Blocks NOT listed here must run clean, except
for prose fragments whose names are defined in the surrounding text, which the gate tolerates
automatically (ol-undefined-var / ol-unknown-command only). Never add an entry to silence a
real defect: kind 'known-broken' records one, so it can be routed to its owner.

docs/design-notes/0001-places-and-value-.why: The record's Context shows the natural-looking syntax OpenLogo rejects; the very next sentence says 'This raises ol-not-a-place'. A clean run here would mean the record no longer describes the language.

docs/design-notes/0006-effect-event-snap.why: DEFECT found by this gate (issue #850): ':x = [1, 2, 3]' separates list items with commas, which OpenLogo has no grammar for — list literals are space-separated ('[1 2 3]'). Recorded rather than fixed here: the record is Status: Accepted, so its edit is routed to @documentation via @orchestrator.
Same defect as the block above, in the second contrasting example of the same section: a comma-separated list literal. Routed, not fixed here.

docs/educational-commands.md.excerpt: # why: debug can show that :size is a word when forward needs a number
docs/educational-commands.md.why: Shows what `debug` explains — ':size = "big"' then 'forward :size'. The paragraph under it quotes the ol-type diagnostic this block must raise.

docs/learn-how-its-built/11-where-you-ty.why: Demonstrates the execution budget itself; the next paragraph quotes the ol-limit line the runtime prints for exactly this program.

spec/commands.md.why: The C3 example for `forever`, whose own 'Possible errors' line is `ol-limit`. It runs until the budget stops it, by definition.

spec/data-structures.md.why: Block comment '# error: the intermediate key tom is missing'. The prose above states that a missing intermediate container raises ol-unknown-key because OpenLogo does not auto-vivify.
Block comment '# error: height is not a person field'. The prose above states that reading or writing an unknown field raises ol-unknown-field.

spec/educational-model.md.excerpt: # why: debug can show that :size is a word when forward needs a number
spec/educational-model.md.why: The same worked `debug` example as docs/educational-commands.md: a word passed to `forward`, which must raise ol-type for the command to have anything to explain.

spec/error-model.md.why: The 'Good diagnostic style' listing: a series of deliberately-wrong programs, each followed by the learner-facing message it must produce. Execution stops at the first runtime error, so only these three codes surface.

spec/grammar.md.why: EBNF production rules for the lexical grammar, fenced as ```logo. The fence language is wrong (```ebnf / ```text), which this gate reports (issue #850) rather than edits: spec/ is maintainer-owned. Asserted so the block cannot change unnoticed while mislabeled.
EBNF production rules for the expression grammar, fenced as ```logo. Same mislabeled-fence defect as the block above; reported, not edited.

spec/interaction-events.md.why: EBNF production rules for the Interaction & Events statements, fenced as ```logo. Same mislabeled-fence defect; reported, not edited.

The `input` example. `input` is the only blocking read in v0.1, and with no host answer available the read ends the only other way spec/interaction-events.md:110-111 allows: the program is cancelled (ol-limit). The block itself is correct OpenLogo.

spec/style-guide.md.excerpt: if :side_count = 4        # syntax error: a condition needs ==, not =
spec/style-guide.md.why: The prose introduces it as 'a syntax error, not merely a style problem' and states the parser 'never finds a delimited body after the condition below and reports ol-missing-end'.
The 'Undelimited bodies' anti-pattern: the prose states that a header followed by instructions with no [ ] block and no `end` is a parse error, even for a single instruction.

spec/tooling.md.why: Layer-1 example: the Finding line under it asserts code=ol-missing-end, stage=parse. Asserting it here keeps the checker's own reference example honest.
Layer-1 example: the Finding line asserts code=ol-bad-token with params={ text: ',' } — commas are not separators in OpenLogo.

Layer-2 example: the Finding line asserts code=ol-unknown-command with a did-you-mean suggestion of `forward`. Listed explicitly — an unlisted misspelling would be auto-tolerated as a prose fragment, and this is precisely the block whose diagnostic must be asserted.
Layer-2 example: the Finding line asserts code=ol-not-enough-inputs for `first` with expected=1, actual=0.
Layer-2 example: the Finding line asserts code=ol-not-a-place. `:nums` is undefined here too, because the block is also an excerpt.
Layer-2 example: the Finding line asserts code=ol-no-value — `map` needs the last instruction in its block to make a value. `:nums` is undefined here too, because the block is also an excerpt.

spec/turtles-and-sprites.md.why: EBNF production rules for the Sprites statements, fenced as ```logo. Same mislabeled-fence defect; reported, not edited.
